title: Geo compliance policy engine: EU residency assertions, tier routing, and fallback model handling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Several enterprise customers and legal reviews require strict controls so that requests flagged as EU-resident data never leave EU jurisdictions. Current smart routing supports region preference but lacks an enforceable policy layer that ties customer contracts, allowlists/denylists, and model variant fallbacks into a single decision path. This ticket implements a policy engine and routing enforcement layer to assert data residency for EU-only contracts and provide predictable fallbacks for capacity or tier constraints.
proposed_solution:
1) Policy engine: central service that evaluates request metadata (customer id, contract flags, explicit 'residency' field, IP geolocation, VPC region) and emits an enforcement decision: ALLOW_IN_REGION, DENY_GLOBAL, REQUIRE_EU_ONLY, or ROUTE_TO_FALLBACK.
2) Tagging: models, nodes, and endpoints are tagged with region labels and compliance capabilities (e.g., eu-resident, pseudonymization-supported, private-only).
3) Routing rules: chain of checks: customer allowlists/denylists -> contract residency flags -> runtime capacity availability in-region -> tier mapping (e.g., platinum can use dedicated EU pool) -> fallback policy. Fallbacks options: a) route to compatible EU-hosted model variant; b) route to customer-dedicated pool (if reserved); c) return structured error with remediation steps; d) queue for delayed processing if policy allows. No data should be mirrored to non-EU endpoints unless explicit customer opt-in recorded.
4) Auditing and attestations: every decision produces an immutable audit event with policy id, decision, inputs, and chosen endpoint. These feed into the Console compliance dashboard and into per-customer logs.
design_decisions:
- Use a fast policy engine (Lua-based rules in the routing daemon) to keep per-request latency under 3ms added overhead.
- Model tag vocabulary: 'residency:eu', 'residency:global', 'private:vpc', 'tier:dedicated'. Keep tags simple to avoid combinatorial explosion.
- Prefer model-variant fallback over returning errors to preserve app availability; however, if the customer contract is strict 'EU-only', fallback must not route outside EU and should return a clear error if no in-region capacity.
- Implement allowlist/denylist at tenant-level: allowlist takes precedence over broader contract flag for experimental customer requests.
- Security review required before enabling auto-fallback for regulated customers.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): implement policy evaluation and audit events behind feature flag. Enable for internal 'GDPR-compliance' org and run synthetic traffic to validate routing decisions (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (pilot): onboard 3 customers with EU residency contracts. Monitor Console compliance dashboard, token-level logs, and SLOs (4 weeks).
Phase 3 (GA): enable self-serve allowlist UI in Console and infra-wide enforcement with blocking fallbacks and alerts (2 weeks).
Rollback plan: disable policy enforcement and fall back to current soft-preference routing; ensure audit events remain stored for post-mortem.
acceptance_criteria:
- Policy engine produces deterministic decisions for all test vectors in the compliance test suite.
- No production requests flagged as EU-only are routed to non-EU endpoints during pilot.
- Audit events are visible in Console with filter by policy id and customer.
- End-to-end added latency from routing decision is <5ms p95.
- Automated tests for allowlist/denylist behaviour and for at-least-one fallback path exist in the routing-infra repo.
